title: On-sale stampede
description: A stadium tour goes on sale at 10:00 with 50,000 seats. Eight million fans are expected within minutes. Holds already use conditional updates, so double sales are impossible, but at the last on-sale the database hit 100% CPU, holds took 20 s, and fans with refresh scripts got most seats. What should you add?

options.text: A virtual waiting room that queues arrivals and admits them with signed, short-lived tokens at a rate matched to measured booking capacity
options.explanation: The booking path sees a steady load it can serve, admission order is controlled rather than won by retry speed, and the token is verified cheaply without a central call.

options.text: Add read replicas and route hold requests to them
options.explanation: Holds are writes that must be decided by the primary; replicas cannot accept them and would risk stale availability decisions.

options.text: Stricter per-IP rate limits at the API gateway
options.explanation: Protects the database somewhat, but random 429s trigger more refreshes, botnets spread across IPs, and there is no fair ordering.

options.text: Move seat holds into Redis with SETNX and write sales to Postgres afterwards
options.explanation: It makes holds faster but creates two sources of truth that can disagree, and it does nothing about unfair access or the flood of requests.
